concerns.text: FR-004 requires comparing the generated plan against a ground-truth plan 'obtained by exhaustive optimal search on a sampled subset of queries' for EVERY query's binary translation error. The plan mentions the exhaustive planner only in prose (Summary item 5, Decision Rationale 8); no phase, task, code module, or data-model entity implements it. Phase 1 runs only the greedy reference_engine, and Phase 2-d defines translation_error as 'disagreement with the deterministic ground_truth_plan'. The exhaustive optimal planner is unbacked by any plan element.

FR-001 mandates 'a strict CPU time limit per query of ≤ 1,000 ms' enforced via cgroups. The plan enforces only a 60-second timeout (FR-003) and a general 'cgroups CPU quota'; the ≤1,000 ms per-query CPU time limit is never specified, configured, or verified anywhere in the plan, research.md, or quickstart.md.

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-009, FR-012 vs contracts/execution_metric.schema.yaml and data-model.md
concerns.text: FR-009 requires computing Precision@10 per query and reporting average precision per source type; FR-012 requires execution_metric to contain 'all latency, translation error, and accuracy fields'. The execution_metric.schema.yaml and the Execution Metric entity in data-model.md omit precision_at_10 entirely (it appears only as a Phase 2-d recording bullet with no computation task, no per-source-type aggregation step, and no schema field).

SC-001 requires 'the ratio of slopes (graph vs. text) estimated via simple linear regression on mean latency per depth is > 1.5'. Phase 3 covers ANOVA, Tukey, chi-square, and the sensitivity sweep but contains no task computing the graph-vs-text slope ratio, so SC-001's second conjunct is unmeasured.

SC-002's second conjunct requires 'the average Precision@10 difference between source types is ≤ 0.02'. research.md §4.2 mentions this threshold but no plan phase or code module (stats.py task list) computes per-source-type average Precision@10 or the between-source difference; the underlying FR-009 computation is itself unbacked (see prior concern).
